items.title: PM Carney bolsters plan to ‘build here’ as companies look to avoid Trump’s latest tariffs
items.author: CTVNews.ca Staff
items.summary: Mark Carney says he is 'always ready' to negotiate with the U.S. in a 'professional' way, after he revealed he had spoken with Donald Trump in recent days.
items.body: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he is “always ready” to negotiate with the U.S. in a “professional” way, after he revealed he had spoken with U.S. President Donald Trump in recent days. On Thursday, Carney signed multiple declarations and initiatives with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Calgary, and later said he plans to “build” in Canada and diversify on an “international level.” Earlier in the day, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre spoke to U.S. media about tariff-free trade between Canada and the U.S. However, he refused to speak negatively about Carney on American soil. This comes after Trump unveiled a flurry of executive orders on Tuesday, restricting trade with Canada the same day Ottawa imposed new countermeasures against the U.S. Despite that, Carney says Canada and the U.S. are still collaborating in other areas. Key details: Here’s what happened on Sept. 10, 2026: Canada is more than the U.S.: Carney As Carney prepares to host an investment summit in Toronto next week, he shared a message to leaders looking to invest in Canada: “We have what the world wants.” “Canada is about so much more than being next to the United States,” he told reporters. “We’re an energy superpower, and we’re putting that into place. We have one of the largest, undeveloped resources of critical metals and minerals.” Carney also elaborated on a list of Canada’s strengths, including its educated population, connected economy and more than a half-billion consumers that he said we’re “on track to double.” Carney did not discourage any businesses or investors from heading to the U.S., but said Canada’s unity, reliability and respect for the rule of law makes it a good partner. “That combination is pretty rare in the world, and it’s an attractive combination.” Kayla Thompson, CTVNews.ca journalist ‘We have a plan’: Carney Speaking to reporters in Calgary, Carney said the federal government has a plan to protect Canadians and businesses as the trade war with the United States intensifies. “Of course, there’s the situation with the U.S. The commercial discussions with the U.S.,” Carney said Thursday evening. “We have a plan. It’s the same plan from the start. We’re going to reinforce it, and the plan is to build, build here.” Carney said the government has been “studying” the new counter-tariff measures from the Americans, but reiterated his plans to build in Canada and “diversify on an international level.” Kayla Thompson, CTVNews.ca journalist Canada ‘always ready to sit down’ with U.S.: Carney When asked whether Carney planned to renegotiate the trade deal with Trump, the prime minister told reporters that Canada is “always ready to sit down in a professional way to negotiate.” Carney did not confirm whether he had plans to negotiate before Trump’s import ban goes into effect on Sep. 29, but said the time in between will be used “to allow for companies to adjust” to the bans. Kayla Thompson, CTVNews.ca journalist ‘It’s just plunder and corruption’: U.S. Rep. Jamie Raskin Speaking with CTV Power Play on Thursday, U.S. Rep. Jamie Raskin said if Canada invested in Trump-related businesses, the U.S. president would drop his tariffs. “If the various Canadian trading partners and negotiators started to make friends with Donald Trump Jr. and the Trump family and do investments with them, this whole thing would go away,” Riskin said during his interview with CTV News Chief Political Correspondent Vassy Kapelos. “I mean, it’s just plunder and corruption that’s taking place here,” he added. Riskin appealed to democratic societies around the world to stand together against what he called “madness” from the Trump administration. Joe Van Wonderen, CTVNews.ca journalist Trump only wants to enrich himself, family: Raskin In his interview with Kapelos, Raskin called for a renewed effort in promoting free trade, going so far as to evoke the name of an 18th century economist. “What’s the theory of free trade, going back to Adam Smith?” he said. “It’s that free countries engaging in free commerce will be able to uplift everybody’s well-being together.” While Raskin cautioned that unfair practices like child and slave labour need to be guarded against, he added that once a government supports basic human rights, it should be able to trade with whomever it sees fit. “And Donald Trump just doesn’t understand the free trade system,” he said. “It’s all about him building as much power for himself and enriching himself and his family as much as he can.” Joe Van Wonderen, CTVNews.ca journalist Carney can’t look into Trump’s soul Taking questions from reporters in Calgary, Carney was asked why he feels Trump appears to be so angry with Canada. “I can’t look deeply into the souls of others,” Carney responded, adding he speaks regularly with the president, and did so within recent days. He also said Canada is “always ready” to strike a fair deal with the U.S. Luca Caruso-Moro, CTVNews.ca journalist Canada working with U.S. despite trade war CTV News Senior Correspondent Judy Trinh asked Carney about Canada’s ability to collaborate with the U.S. to achieve peace in Ukraine while engaged in a trade war. “We can compartmentalize,” the prime minister responded, adding his team is in constant communication with the Americans on topics outside of trade, including Iran. “That’s part of our responsibility,” he said. Luca Caruso-Moro, CTVNews.ca journalist ‘A matter of how long it’s going to take’: Hoekstra United States Ambassador Pete Hoekstra told CTV News that said they don’t “refer to it as a trade war,” when asked about the ongoing tariff battle between Canada and the U.S. Hoekstra, who is visiting Gander, N.L. to attend a Sept. 11 ceremony on Friday, claimed some Canadian politicians regretted the things they had said amid the feud. “Let’s talk about the issue here. Let’s get (it) resolved and let’s move it forward. But now, for the next two or three days, we’re here to remember what happened 25 years ago,” he said on Thursday, referring to the quarter-century anniversary of the terror attack on New York City. “I’m not going to get into the trade stuff here. I’ve been out of the loop now for you know four or five hours. Who knows what’s happened in the last four or five hours?” Hoesktra added. “We’re talking about 9/11. These other things will come back. We’ll have to deal with them. They’ll get resolved. We’re going to move forward. It’s just a matter of how long it’s going to take.” Aarjavee Raaj, CTVNews.ca journalist Read Graham Richardson’s full story Canada cozying up with China: Trump aide An American economist and aide to Trump says Canada is not fighting as an equal in the ongoing trade war. In an article published in Real Clear Markets, Peter Navarro compares Canada to a rowboat opening fire on an aircraft carrier. “The carrier will notice. The rowboat will sink,” Navarro wrote, saying Canada is cozying up with “the mercantilist and predatory dog of Communist China” as it works to broaden its trading relationships. “Not going to happen. Not on Trump’s watch,” he wrote. “O Canada. Make the smart move now. We’re not budging.” The Canadian Press Carney wants to build millions of drones Carney says Canada will expand its drone arsenal to include millions of unmanned vehicles within the next two years. It’s part of a new plan that will combine Ukrainian battlefield experience with domestic manufacturing and AI, he said. He made the announcement alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Calgary, where the two leaders signed a 100-year collaboration agreement Thursday. Carney also said Canada would establish a national drone marketplace to supply national military units with drone technology. Under the plan, one-third of all drones manufactured in Canada will supply Ukrainian’s defence effort. Canada’s drone arsenal presently includes about 2,000 units, said Carney. Luca Caruso-Moro, CTVNews.ca journalist Canada to join Freya project Carney is confirming a new partnership with the EU, that will have Canada join Freya, a pan-European anti-ballistic missile defence project. The development comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Canada and the EU were working to build a new all-encompassing alliance that will include trade, security, supply chains and critical raw materials. Carney told reporters that Canada’s involvement will support Ukraine, but is “also indicative of Canada’s deepening relationship with European partners.” Carney said he and the EU will “have more to say to that in Strasbourg” when he visits the European Parliament in France, next week. Kayla Thompson, CTVNews.ca journalist ‘100% zoned in on the tariffs:’ Ford Ontario Premier Doug Ford has shuffled his cabinet into what he called a “good team” to “fight the tariffs” and to “fight President Trump.” “You’ve seen a lot of action over the last few weeks, actually, probably last month or so with President Trump, but we need a strong, strong plan to continue what we’re working on right all summer,” Ford told reporters on Thursday morning. “Actually, and I just want to emphasize: without a break, there were no breaks, no going anywhere, I’m 100 per cent zoned in on the tariffs and on President Trump.” Ford said he looks forward to working with the prime minister on their “strong plan” to keep moving forward, “continue prospering, continue giving people hope in Ontario, even with the tariffs coming at us.” “We’re targeted over any jurisdiction because our manufacturing might, our technology, agricultural, financial, quite a few different areas that were the engine of Canada,” Ford said. “So, obviously, we’re going to be targeted, but we’ll continue fighting back and making sure we have a strong, vibrant area to invest right around the world.” Alex Arsenych, CTVNewsToroto.ca journalist Grocers prepared for tariffs Grocery chains are less impacted by the tariffs this time around, executives from the grocery chain Empire Co. Ltd. say. While the grocery retailer has received some requests from suppliers to raise prices, chief customer officer Luc L’Archevêque said it hasn’t accepted any so far. “ ... it’s too early, so we won’t accept any cost increases related to tariffs, and we’ll work very closely with our supplier partners to find solutions,” he told analysts during the company’s fiscal first-quarter earnings call on Thursday. After last year’s tariff war, grocery chains established stronger relationships with local and non-U.S. suppliers to offer more alternatives to tariffed food items and better respond to a resurgence of the buy Canadian sentiment among shoppers. “We have a large assortment, so customers can make many different choices to avoid U.S. products,” Empire’s chief executive Pierre St-Laurent said. The Canadian Press Canada could be richest country on Earth: Poilievre Poilievre appeared on CNBC this morning to push for tariff-free trade between Canada and the U.S. “We can be the richest country in the world,” he said during an interview, heralding Canada’s expansive coastline, potash exports, oil reserves and farmland. He also advocated for reduced taxes, shortened permitting and to “unleash free enterprise” in Canada. Dropping tariffs, he also said, would benefit both Canada and the U.S. “If we believe in free markets then we have to believe in free trade.” Luca Caruso-Moro, CTVNews.ca journalist Carney meets Zelenskyy in Calgary Carney is sitting down for a closed-door meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Calgary, Alta. During brief remarks to reporters in the room before talks began, the prime minister reiterated Canada’s support for the country, which was invaded by Russia in February 2022. So far, Canada has provided $26 billion in military and humanitarian support, said Carney, who pledged to provide more. He also said Canada supports Ukraine’s “path” to join NATO and the EU. “Ukraine’s future is for Ukrainians only to decide,” he also said. Luca Caruso-Moro, CTVNews.ca journalist ‘It’s just plunder and corruption’: U.S. Rep. Jamie Raskin A U.S. Congress Representative said that if Canada invested in Trump-related businesses, the U.S. president would drop his tariffs. Speaking to CTV News Power Play on Thursday, Jamie Riskin suggested that the U.S. would be friendlier with Canada, if Ottawa invested in Trump-connected businesses. “If the various Canadian trading partners and negotiators started to make friends with Donald Trump Jr. and the Trump family and do investments with them, this whole thing would go away,” Riskin said. “I mean its just plunder and corruption that’s taking place here,” he added. Riskin appealed to democratic societies around the world to stand together against what he called “madness” from the Trump regime. Joe Van Wonderen, CTVNews.ca journalist MapQuest posts billboard with directions to Lake Ontario MapQuest is doubling down on its decision to continue to keep Lake Ontario on its map with a six-foot billboard in Chicago. The billboard features directions on how to get from there to Lake Ontario, with the campaign line: “It’s still Lake Ontario. And we’re still here.” The billboard is a response to Trump’s signing of an executive order to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America” last month. CNN Read the full story here Brampton, Ont. unveils 10-point tariff action plan The City of Brampton, Ont. has unveiled a 10-point plan of action in an effort to mitigate the impacts of U.S. tariffs. Mayor Patrick Brown described it as a “practical plan to protect jobs, help businesses compete, and build a stronger local economy.” Brown said the “economic resilience” plan will focus on three pillars: protect, protect, compete, and build. He said the plan will entail a range of measures, including protecting local jobs, businesses and manufacturing, fostering productivity and growth, diversifying trade, attracting investment, unlocking incentives, accelerating infrastructure projects, and mobilizing cross-border support “This action plan is about positioning our businesses to compete. This plan is about protecting jobs while building a stronger economy for tomorrow,” Brown said during a news conference late Thursday morning at Brampton City Hall. Joanna Lavoie, CP24.com journalist ‘The time to act is now’: N.B. premier New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt says the province is taking action to support local businesses, jobs and products amid the trade war. Announced Thursday, the series of measures aims to steer public spending toward domestic products, helping businesses diversify into new markets and provide financial support to companies feeling the impact of the latest tariffs. “The time to act is now,” Holt told reporters. Starting Oct. 1, the provincial government plans to prohibit the procurement of U.S. goods or services for significant contracts (estimated value over $5 million), among other measures. Find the full list here. Melanie Price, CTVNewsAtlantic.ca journalist Trade war impacts integrated supply chain: Michigan executive With counter-tariffs now in effect, the ongoing feud between Canada and the U.S. is “damaging the economics” of a very integrated auto supply chain, according to a Detroit automotive executive. “Both of our countries going back and forth is not helping something that has been built for decades and is stronger together,” Glenn Stevens Jr., executive director of MichAuto at the Detroit Regional Chamber, told CTV News channel on Thursday. He added that the input costs are rising from both, the company and the customers’ perspectives, calling the new tariffs “above and beyond” CUSMA. According to Stevens Jr., the consumers are going to feel the increase in prices, leading to lower demands and job cutbacks. He said they were hoping for not only a resolution, but a stronger trade agreement between the two countries. “This really hurts companies’ inputs, and ultimately somebody has to pay for them, and that unfortunately winds up being the consumer,” he added, arguing that Canada, the U.S., and Mexico are stronger together against competition from China. “We look at our partners and our friends literally across the river from my office here as not just trade partners, but we literally build things together and have been doing that for a long time,” Stevens Jr. said. Aarjavee Raaj, CTVNews.ca journalist Building ferries in B.C. would help trade battle; report A new report says building ferries in British Columbia would help the province weather the harsh economic trade winds coming from the United States. The report from the Centre of Future Work says building ferries in local shipyards rather than purchasing them from foreign ones would help the provincial and Canadian economy grapple with steep American tariffs. A coalition of unions and industry leaders commissioned the report, which appears 15 months after BC Ferries announced it had contracted a shipyard owned by the Chinese government to build four major vessels at a cost that’s yet to be disclosed. The ferry operator, which is overseen by the B.C. Ferry Authority, said at the time that no Canadian company had submitted a proposal and the winning bid from China Merchants Weihai Shipyards was at least $1 billion cheaper than others. The Canadian Press, Read the full article here Carney playing ‘cool’ to Trump: Mulcair A former NDP leader says Carney’s “muted response” to Trump’s actions over the last day is a “wise” move. Tom Mulcair told CTV News Channel on Thursday that Canada has “entered a twilight zone with Trump.” “This is no longer chaos, this is insanity,” he described of Trump’s announcement to award $5,000 to individuals if he won in the upcoming elections. Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre can lend a strong Conservative voice if he is more “statesman-like” instead of “trying to make it partisan,” Mulcair added. “We do want to integrate our economies, but not at the expense of being beholden to the United States the way they tried to,” he said. Devika Desai, CTVNews.ca journalist Trade deal ‘would have destroyed our economy’: Ford Ontario Premier Doug Ford says Carney was right to walk away from an “absolutely terrible deal” with the U.S. that “would have destroyed our economy from top to bottom.” Ford made the comment during a speech at the Toronto Region Board of Trade on Thursday, where he also announced expanded eligibility for a $1-billion tariff relief program for impacted businesses and workers in Ontario. “It was a deal that would have hurt Canadian workers, undermined Canadian sovereignty and caused permanent damage to Canadian businesses that employ hundreds of thousands of workers across our country and province,” Ford said. He added he supports Carney’s decision to respond to the latest U.S. tariffs with “dollar-for-dollar” counter-tariffs but warned “we have to be prepared to withstand the pain” that comes with showing Trump “Canada will stand up for itself.” “If you don’t stand up for a bully they will continue to bully,” he said. Chris Fox, CTVNewsToronto.ca journalist Effect of U.S. motorcycle ban? A Quebec manufacturer says the U.S. ban on Canadian motorcycles will have a “limited” impact on the upcoming fiscal year. Moto Canada president and CEO Landon French told CTV Your Morning on Thursday that the “vast majority of production and shipments for the current season are completed.” However, French says the current trade war has the potential to “cost jobs,” decrease product choice and increase prices. It could also make it more difficult for dealerships to supply custom-made inventory. “Eventually we need a deal,” he said. Devika Desai, CTVNews.ca journalist Trump’s Canada-bashing echoed at U.S. convention Thousands of U.S. President Donald Trump’s most ardent followers have gathered in Dallas for “Trump-a-Palooza” this week and many are parroting the president’s constant bashing of Canada. Lona Heins from Tennessee says Canada is now “communist” and no longer shares the same values as the United States. Heins says she needs more information about bilateral trade tensions, which were escalated by the Trump administration on Tuesday, but hopes the situation can be resolved. The Canadian Press, Read the full story here Trump pledges US$5,000 payments if GOP wins Trump pledged Wednesday to send every American adult US$5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, an extraordinary gambit to reverse his party’s sagging fortunes in November. The dubious promise would likely cost more than $1 trillion and require congressional approval, and would further exacerbate the country’s nearly $1.8 trillion annual budget deficit and concerns about inflation. “If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000,” Trump said during the GOP’s midterm convention in Dallas. “It will be called the Trump Dividend.” Within an hour, Vice President JD Vance appeared to try to walk back Trump’s proposal -- at least in part -- by suggesting the dividend payments would not go to the wealthy. Vance suggested it could be paid for by U.S. tariff revenues, though the suggested payment dwarfs what the U.S. has taken in through the protectionist measures. The Associated Press Here’s what happened on Sept. 9, 2026: Canada scales back energy project reviews The federal government is scaling back a major Trudeau-era environmental review process, removing several energy projects from the federal impact assessment regime and shifting responsibility for their review to the Canada Energy Regulator (CER). The federal government said the change will “simplify the project decision process” by relying on a single federal regulator. “Industry stakeholders expressed strong support for the proposal to have all pipeline projects reviewed exclusively by the CER. Industry actors view this as a key step toward improving regulatory certainty, reducing duplication, and streamlining approvals,” the federal government said in its regulatory impact analysis. The move comes just as Carney gets set to lead the Canada Investment Summit in Toronto next week. It is the federal government’s attempt to attract major infrastructure investments in Canada with a goal of $1 trillion in new investment over the next five years. Graham Richardson, CTV News Ottawa Bureau chief. Read the full story here. Canada in ‘strong fiscal position’: finance minister Speaking at the Edmonton Chamber of Commerce on Wednesday, Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne appeared confident that Canada would weather the storm from the U.S. trade war as it builds partnerships around the world. “I see a golden opportunity in front of us,” he said. “The world is changing. America is changing. The world energy architecture is changing, and in that new world … Canada can be at the centre. Why? Because we provide stability, predictability, and trust.” Champagne also discussed Alberta projects, Canada’s global partnerships and his efforts to help affordability for Canadians. “We have strong fiscal position to support people,” he said. “That’s the package announced: $7.5 billion, making sure that we can provide liquidity quickly to small- and medium-sized businesses, and at the same time support affected workers.” Elianna Lev, CTVNews.ca multi-platform writer Canada ‘dying’ to make a deal: Trump Trump said Canada wants to make a deal with the United States while delivering his keynote address at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas Wednesday night. During his speech, Trump brought up his administration’s decision to rename bodies of water, which include changing Lake Ontario to “Lake America” and the Gulf of Mexico to the “Gulf of America.” “Lake Ontario, we’re now going to call that Lake America,” Trump said. “Canada very much wants to make a deal, they’re dying to make a deal. But it’s going to be called Lake America.” Trump then brought up his suggestion to change the name of New Mexico, a Democrat-led U.S. state, to “New America.” Hunter Crowther, CTVNews.ca journalist Trump’s ‘pointless’ trade war: Democrat senators U.S. Democratic Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Chris Coons, Patty Murray, Amy Klobuchar and Elissa Slotkin say in a joint statement that the states they represent rely on Canada as a key trading partner. They say Trump is doubling down on a “pointless” trade war. “His tariffs will squeeze our states’ small businesses harder and drive costs up for working families,” they say. “President Trump’s tariffs have already cost American families as much as $5,000 in some states, and his senseless trade war with Canada will only grow that number.” The senators say partners around the world, including Canada, are increasingly looking to diversify away from the United States and deepen trade ties with other countries, including China. “Congressional Republicans need to stand up to the president and do their part to give families and businesses on both sides of the border relief from this insanity,” says the statement. The Canadian Press Greer gave LeBlanc notice of Trump’s orders: source According to a source close to the trade discussions, Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc was given a short heads up from U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer before Trump’s executive orders were made public last night. The source tells CTV News it was a short “cordial” text exchange via messages, however, LeBlanc and Greer did not speak over the phone. Mike Le Couteur, CTV News senior political correspondent Poilievre heads to U.S. to promote Canada Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is heading to New York and will participate in ceremonies commemorating the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks Friday, according to a senior Conservative source. According to the source, the trip is being carried out with the blessing of the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). Poilievre wanted to go to the United States earlier, but the PMO advised at the time such a visit would be unhelpful. CTV News reached out to the PMO for comment but did not receive an immediate response. Abigail Bimman, CTV News correspondent. Read the full story here.

items.title: Petrol and diesel prices today – 11 Sep: Fuel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru as Crude oil extends rally
items.author: Fareha Naaz
items.summary: Petrol and diesel prices today – 11 Sep: Check fuel rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and other cities as crude oil extended rally amid renewed Houthis attacks on Saudi oil facilities and recovery in Chinese oil demand.
items.body: Petrol and diesel prices today, 11 September: Fuel rates across Indian cities witnessed slight changes on Friday, 11 September, but continue to align with 25 May price adjustment. The global benchmark Brent crude extended its rally amid escalation in fighting in West Asia as Iran-backed Houthi militants intensified strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure.State-run Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) that follow dynamic fuel price method continue to insulate domestic customers from volatility in international energy prices. Even though fuel rates in India are revised daily at 6:00 AM but they remain steady and mirror the last major price adjustment when petrol and diesel were increased by ₹2.7 to ₹2.8 per litre, respectively. Hence, commodity prices have been stable for over three months despite significant fluctuation in global energy prices. Check latest petrol and diesel prices in your city on 11 September.Crude oil price todayAccording to Bloomberg, Brent crude surged 0.4% on Friday after rising 6% to almost $110 a barrel in US trading and is on track for the biggest weekly gain since July. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude edged 0.9% higher to trade around $103.40 a barrel.RBC Capital Markets LLC analyst Helima Croft reacted to Houthis advancement to one of the world’s most vital straits and said that it “would allow the group to project its disruptive capabilities further south towards the narrowest points of the waterway.” She added, “A resumption of a full-blown Saudi-Houthi war would be a potential catalyst for our high oil price scenario coming to fruition,” Bloomberg reported.US-Iran war news updateUS President Donald Trump on Thursday (local time) said that he doesn't regret the ongoing Iran war despite the impact the conflict may have on the November US midterm elections. This statement comes at a time Washington renewed attacks against Tehran, with the Islamic Republic retaliating by launching strikes across the US bases in West Asia.Injecting fresh risk into the market and stoking fears of deeper supply disruptions, Houthis advanced toward coastal areas bordering the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, gaining ground in their attempt to seize Mokha near the southern end of the Red Sea. Dangers to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint persist as two ships were struck by unidentified projectiles west of Khasab, Oman, on Thursday as reported by the UK Maritime Trade Operations.Operations at some Saudi energy facilities has come to a halt since resumption of Houthi attacks over the past two weeks. An increase in crude purchases by China also influenced oil prices. Brent crude jumped almost 80% this year but remains below its wartime peak of $126 a barrel reached in April.Commodities economist at Capital Economics Ltd commodities economist Hamad Hussain said, “Market participants appear to be revising their expectations for the severity and duration of the war in Iran." He further noted that renewed disruption in West Asia flows could potentially push prices back toward recent peaks amid depleting global inventories and recovery of Chinese demand.

items.title: Ebola Reaches Congo’s Sud-Ubangi Province After Patient Traveled Through Rwanda and Uganda
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: Ebola has now spread to a seventh province in the Democratic Republic of Congo after a 23-year-old man tested positive for the virus following a cross-country journey that included travel through neighboring Rwanda and Uganda.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- Ebola has now spread to a seventh province in the Democratic Republic of Congo after a 23-year-old man tested positive for the virus following a cross-country journey that included travel through neighboring Rwanda and Uganda.The man died in Gwaka in the northwestern province of Sud-Ubangi after testing positive for the Bundibugyo strain of ebolavirus, said Jean-Jacques Mbungani, a former Congolese health minister and national lawmaker. Provincial authorities declared an Ebola outbreak Thursday after the case was confirmed by Congo’s National Institute of Biomedical Research, local news outlet Identité News and Xinhua reported.The man had left Kamanyola in South Kivu and traveled over about three weeks through Rwanda and Uganda before returning to Congo and passing through Aru, Bunia, Kisangani, Bumba, Lisala and Akula on his way to Gwaka, Mbungani said in a social media post Thursday. The journey included river travel and potentially exposed numerous people, he said. The case extends an outbreak previously confined to an area roughly the size of the UK and raises fresh concerns about the virus spreading along Congo’s heavily traveled transport corridors. Ebola can cause severe vomiting and diarrhea, leading to dehydration, shock and multi-organ failure. Almost half of confirmed cases in the outbreak have been fatal.Congo had recorded 6,942 confirmed infections and 3,349 deaths through Wednesday. The epidemic had reached 61 health zones across six provinces before the Sud-Ubangi case was confirmed.Transmission has been easing in several hotspots in Ituri, the original epicenter, while accelerating in North Kivu, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention told media Thursday.North Kivu accounted for 46 of the 99 new infections reported Wednesday, almost matching Ituri’s 47, according to Congo’s National Institute for Public Health. Ebola treatment facilities in North Kivu were operating at 132% of available bed capacity, the institute said in a report Thursday.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.title: Chris Kreider becomes free agent after Ducks terminate contract
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Anaheim Ducks terminated forward Chris Kreider's contract on Thursday after he went unclaimed on unconditional waivers.
items.body:
The Anaheim Ducks terminated forward Chris Kreider's contract on Thursday after he went unclaimed on unconditional waivers.
Kreider, 35, is now an unrestricted free agent with league training camps set to open next week. He had one season left -- at a $6.5 million average annual value against the salary cap -- on a seven-year, $45.5 million extension he signed while with the New York Rangers in February 2020.
The Ducks said the move gives them more financial flexibility under the salary cap. They are trying to re-sign restricted free agent forward Cutter Gauthier, 22, who led the team with 41 goals and 69 points last season.
"I want to thank Chris for his efforts last year and recognize the professionalism he and his representatives demonstrated throughout this process," Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek said. "Our rationale here is straightforward: We needed to create salary cap flexibility, and this accomplishes that."
The Ducks matched a five-year, $90 million offer sheet sent to star center Leo Carlsson by the Philadelphia Flyers in July -- with his $18 million average annual value the highest for any NHL player this coming season. The team also signed forward A.J. Greer to a four-year deal and defenseman Pavel Mintyukov to a five-year contract this summer.
Kreider recorded 50 points (22 goals, 28 assists) in 75 games during his only season with Anaheim in 2025-26. He added seven points (two goals, five assists) in 12 playoff games.
He played his first 13 NHL seasons with the New York Rangers, who drafted him in the first round (19th overall) in 2009. He has 632 points (348 goals, 284 assists), 609 penalty minutes and a plus-117 rating in 958 career games with New York (2012-25) and Anaheim.
Kreider led the NHL with 26 power-play goals and 11 game-winning goals during the 2021-22 season, when he scored a career-high 52 goals.
The Rangers traded him to the Ducks in June 2025 with a fourth-round draft pick for forward prospect Carey Terrance and a third-round selection that year.
Kreider has 83 points (50 goals, 33 assists) in 135 career playoff games.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Sydney Airport flights disrupted due to air traffic controller shortage
items.author: Renju Jose
items.creator: Renju Jose
items.summary: A shortage of air traffic controllers caused flight cancellations and delays at Sydney Airport on Friday morning, the federal agency responsible for managing Australia's air traffic said, as probes continue into several recent near-misses at the airport.
items.body:
A shortage of air traffic controllers caused flight cancellations and delays at Sydney Airport on Friday morning, the federal agency responsible for managing Australia's air traffic said, as probes continue into several recent near-misses at the airport.
Airservices Australia said it was required to enact Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) measures at Sydney Airport "due to roster constraints" and "to safely manage aviation demand."
The ATFM measures were lifted at 8:15 a.m. (2215 GMT on Thursday) after conditions improved, though delays of no more than 10 minutes were still expected for the rest of the morning.
"Airservices acknowledges the ATFM measures may have caused some disruptions to airline scheduling, and is working with airlines to reduce delays and the impact on passenger travel as much as possible," a spokesperson said by email.
The agency said it was taking steps to recruit more air traffic controllers and make it easier to call on additional staff when needed.
Some Qantas (QAN.AX) flights faced delays of more than an hour, and six flights were cancelled. Sydney Airport's website did not specify a reason for the delays, and a spokesperson referred enquiries to Airservices Australia.
The disruptions come as Airservices Australia CEO Rob Sharp and other senior executives are due to appear later on Friday before a Senate committee that is examining the state of Australia's aviation sector and its ability to deliver reliable and affordable services to regional areas.
Last week, a Reuters [USN:L6N44V00A TEXT:"report"] — citing internal records and a call recording — said several air traffic controllers on duty when two Qantas aircraft nearly collided at Sydney Airport in July had been flagged as facing a high risk of fatigue.
One shift manager reportedly described the staffing situation as "a bit insane."
That incident was the first of six [USN:L4N44I02N TEXT:"near-misses"] at Sydney Airport in the space of about a month, prompting further scrutiny of air traffic control staffing amid global shortages. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating the close calls to determine whether they shared common safety issues or contributing factors.

items.title: Snapchat lanza Snapchat Plans, una herramienta para organizar encuentros con amigos: así funciona
items.author: Alexandra Levine
items.summary: Snapchat Plans, basado en la idea de que aproximadamente un tercio de los jóvenes que usan la aplicación en Estados Unidos hacen planes a través de chats grupales y mensajes directos, es un conjunto d ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Snap Inc. ( SNAP ) ha lanzado nuevas funciones de planificación de eventos que permiten a los usuarios de Snapchat organizar reuniones con amigos, enviar invitaciones y recopilar respuestas sin salir de la aplicación. Snapchat Plans, basado en la idea de que aproximadamente un tercio de los jóvenes que usan la aplicación en Estados Unidos hacen planes a través de chats grupales y mensajes directos, es un conjunto de herramientas que “ayuda a los amigos a convertir las conversaciones en encuentros en persona”, desde fiestas de cumpleaños hasta sesiones de estudio, según informó la compañía en una publicación de blog el jueves. Estas reuniones, que pueden incluir hasta 200 amigos, son privadas y solo por invitación. Una nueva sección llamada “Mis planes” en los perfiles de los usuarios les permitirá hacer un seguimiento de todos sus compromisos en un solo lugar. Ver más: Meta presiona a TikTok, YouTube y Snap por seguridad de adolescentes tras acuerdo con estados de EE.UU. La herramienta de programación es la última expansión de productos de Snapchat, que va más allá de las publicaciones efímeras por las que es más conocida. La compañía ha introducido productos de suscripción, como Snapchat+, que ofrece funciones exclusivas, y Memories, un plan de almacenamiento para imágenes y videos, que han ayudado a reducir su dependencia de la publicidad. El 16 de septiembre, Snap también comenzará a vender su primer par de gafas de realidad aumentada, las Specs, por US$2.195. Snap ofreció unas previsiones optimistas para el periodo actual durante su último informe de resultados el mes pasado, lo que denota optimismo de cara al lanzamiento comercial de estos dispositivos wearables basados en inteligencia artificial. Snap también está tomando medidas para diferenciarse de otras plataformas de redes sociales como Meta Platforms Inc. ( META ), YouTube de Google y TikTok, todas ellas demandadas en litigios nacionales de gran envergadura que las acusan de diseñar deliberadamente sus productos para que fueran adictivos para los usuarios jóvenes. Snap ha emprendido una cruzada para demostrar al mundo que no son redes sociales y que Snapchat fue concebida como una alternativa desde sus inicios. Ver más: Snap eleva la previsión de ventas antes de lanzar sus gafas de realidad aumentada “TikTok tiene tendencias, Meta tiene alcance y Snapchat te conoce de verdad”, afirmó el CEO Evan Spiegel en su carta anual, publicada esta semana. “Esto se debe a que cuando algo realmente nos importa, nos hacemos una foto, se lo contamos a un amigo o nos presentamos en persona. Esos son los comportamientos básicos en Snapchat y parte de lo que hace que nuestro servicio sea único”. Snapchat Plans parece ser una parte de esa estrategia más amplia, que anima a los usuarios a pasar de hablar de encuentros por mensajes a organizar reuniones presenciales. Pero también podría aumentar la interacción dentro de la propia aplicación. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: California enacts new curbs on social media for children
items.author: Steve Gorman
items.creator: Steve Gorman
items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law on Thursday new tech company restrictions barring children under 16 from exposure to behaviorally addictive features on social media platforms and banning toys containing AI companion chatbots.
items.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law on Thursday new tech company restrictions barring children under 16 from exposure to behaviorally addictive features on social media platforms and banning toys containing AI companion chatbots.
The two measures were among 13 bills Newsom enacted as a package designed to safeguard young people from technology seen as putting them at risk, including greater online privacy protection for minors.
Another measure expanded the scope of criminal sanctions against child sexual abuse material to include any digitally altered or AI-generated content that depicts a person under the age of 18 engaged in sexual conduct.
Still another bans for the next four years the manufacture and sale of toys that incorporate a companion chatbot. A related measure requires parental controls on chatbot programs, along with other safety and risk assessments.
Newsom touted those regulations as the most far-reaching of their kind in the nation. The bill was dubbed "Adam's Law," in memory of [USN:L6N3UI0O3 TEXT:"Adam Raine"], a 16-year-old boy who took his own life in April 2025 after he acted, according to his parents, on suicidal thoughts validated in months of discussion with OpenAI's ChatGPT program.
OpenAI has said it intends to improve ChatGPT safeguards, which the company has acknowledged became "less reliable" as user interactions grow more prolonged.
"We want our children - and every California kid - to grow up in a world where technology supports their wellbeing, rather than exploits their vulnerabilities," Newsom, a Democrat, said in a statement announcing the measures.
California, home of such leading internet companies as Google , Meta Platforms (META.O) and Snap Inc (SNAP.N) , joins a [USN:L6N44B10Y TEXT:"growing list of U.S. states"] cracking down on business strategies seen as deliberately designed to hook teenagers on social media, despite evidence that extensive use is harmful to their mental health.
While gaining broad bipartisan support, some critics objected to the bill as an unnecessary restriction on young people's internet access, including the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which called the bill "a massive privacy and free speech nightmare."
Utah became the first to adopt laws regulating children's access to social media, followed by others, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Ohio, Texas, Florida and New York, though approaches have varied.
'PSYCHOLOGICALLY EXPLOITATIVE' FEATURES TARGETED [USN:L6N44L075 TEXT:"Countries around the world"] have also moved to curb children's access to harmful internet content, including a [USN:L1N430003 TEXT:"ban in Australia"] on social media for children under 16.
California's version, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits children under age 16 from exposure to a number of "psychologically exploitative features intended to maximize engagement that foreseeably lead to compulsive use."
Those include infinite-scroll feeds, algorithmic autoplay and other features to be defined in future regulations.
Its enactment comes at a time when Big Tech, in the face of mounting legal challenges, has shown greater willingness to accept new restrictions.
[USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"Meta agreed"] three weeks ago to pay as much as $18 billion over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use its Facebook and Instagram platforms under a deal with nearly all U.S. states to resolve civil claims that the company designed its social media platforms to addict children.

LOS ANGELES, Sept 10 : California Governor Gavin Newsom signed into law on Thursday new tech company restrictions barring children under 16 from exposure to behaviorally addictive features on social media platforms and banning toys containing AI companion chatbots.
The two measures were among 13 bills Newsom enacted as a package designed to safeguard young people from technology seen as putting them at risk, including greater online privacy protection for minors.
Another measure expanded the scope of criminal sanctions against child sexual abuse material to include any digitally altered or AI-generated content that depicts a person under the age of 18 engaged in sexual conduct.

Newsom touted those regulations as the most far-reaching of their kind in the nation. The bill was dubbed "Adam's Law," in memory of Adam Raine, a 16-year-old boy who took his own life in April 2025 after he acted, according to his parents, on suicidal thoughts validated in months of discussion with OpenAI's ChatGPT program.
OpenAI has said it intends to improve ChatGPT safeguards, which the company has acknowledged became "less reliable" as user interactions grow more prolonged.
"We want our children - and every California kid - to grow up in a world where technology supports their wellbeing, rather than exploits their vulnerabilities," Newsom, a Democrat, said in a statement announcing the measures.
California, home of such leading internet companies as Google, Meta Platforms and Snap Inc, joins a growing list of U.S. states cracking down on business strategies seen as deliberately designed to hook teenagers on social media, despite evidence that extensive use is harmful to their mental health.
While gaining broad bipartisan support, some critics objected to the bill as an unnecessary restriction on young people's internet access, including the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which called the bill "a massive privacy and free speech nightmare."
Utah became the first to adopt laws regulating children's access to social media, followed by others, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Ohio, Texas, Florida and New York, though approaches have varied.
'PSYCHOLOGICALLY EXPLOITATIVE' FEATURES TARGETED
Countries around the world have also moved to curb children's access to harmful internet content, including a ban in Australia on social media for children under 16. 
California's version, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits children under age 16 from exposure to a number of "psychologically exploitative features intended to maximize engagement that foreseeably lead to compulsive use." 
Those include infinite-scroll feeds, algorithmic autoplay and other features to be defined in future regulations.
Its enactment comes at a time when Big Tech, in the face of mounting legal challenges, has shown greater willingness to accept new restrictions. 
Meta agreed three weeks ago to pay as much as $18 billion over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use its Facebook and Instagram platforms under a deal with nearly all U.S. states to resolve civil claims that the company designed its social media platforms to addict children.

items.title: 原油先物は1％高、100ドル台維持　週間で約13％急伸
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [シンガポール １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[シンガポール １１日 ロイター] - １１日アジア時間の原油先物は続伸し、主要２指標はともに１バレル＝１００ドルを超えて今週の取引を終える見通しとなっている。週間ベースで１００ドルを上回るのは５月中旬以来。中東の主要な海上輸送路への攻撃が増加し、供給の混乱が長期化するとの懸念が高まっている。

００４５ＧＭＴ（日本時間午前９時４５分）時点で、北海ブレント先物は１．０５ドル（１％）高の１バレル＝１０８．６８ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は０．９５ドル（同じく１％）高の１０３．４５ドル。１０日は両指標とも６％超上昇した。

週間ベースでは両指標とも１３％近く値上がりしており、上昇率としては７月１７日までの週以来の大きさとなっている。

イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は１０日、西部の戦略的な港湾都市モカを掌握し、紅海の海上交通に一段の脅威となっている。一方、ペルシャ湾では最近のタンカー攻撃の激化を受け、ホルムズ海峡経由の航行が引き続き制限されている。

アナリストによると、イエメンからのサウジアラビアのエネルギー施設への攻撃は、イランとホルムズ海峡の枠を超えたエスカレーションを示すもので、より広い地域で混乱が長期化するとの懸念を高めている。

トランプ米大統領は９日、イラン中部ナタンズのウラン濃縮施設近くにある「ピックアックス山」を攻撃する可能性があると警告した。また、戦争は１１月の中間選挙後に終結するとの見方を示した。

ＩＧのアナリスト、トニー・シカモア氏は「情勢が悪化し、イランがこの紛争を可能な限り広く、長く引き延ばす姿勢を見せる中、ＷＴＩが３月初旬の高値である１１９．４８ドルを再び試す可能性が高まっている」と述べた。

イランは、米国が同国の石油タンカー５隻を攻撃した後、９日にホルムズ海峡付近で船舶１０隻を攻撃したと表明した。イラン革命防衛隊は、さらなる攻撃があれば対応をエスカレートさせるとしている。

価格追跡サービスのガスバディーによると、米国のディーゼル燃料の全国平均価格は１０日、初めて１ガロン＝６ドルを突破した。米・イラン戦争のほか、ウクライナによるロシア製油所への攻撃が供給を圧迫している。

アナリストらは、上昇相場が持続するかどうかは、世界最大の原油輸入国である中国次第だと指摘。中国が買いを継続すれば、供給の混乱の影響が増幅され、価格をさらに押し上げる可能性がある。

石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）は１０日公表した月報で、２０２６年の世界石油需要の見通しを日量３８万バレル増に引き下げた。下方修正は５カ月連続となる。

items.title: Ｆ１＝接触事故のフェラーリ勢、わだかまり解消　交戦規定明文化せず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［マドリード　１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［マドリード　１０日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１のフェラーリ勢、シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）とルイス・ハミルトン（英国）は、先週末のイタリア・グランプリ（ＧＰ）で起きた接触事故について話し合い、わだかまりを解消したと明かした。

ハミルトンはオープニングラップでルクレールにコース外のグラベル（砂利）に押し出され、４番手から１０番手に後退。最終的に６位で終えたレース後、交戦ルールを明文化するように求めていた。

１０日に行われたスペインＧＰの会見で、ハミルトンは「私と彼、２人だけで向かい合って話し合った」とルクレールと対話したことを明かし、「お互いに率直かつ正直に話し、問題を解決した。これで前に進むことができる。健全なことだと思う。時間をかけて築き上げてきた関係だ。お互いに勝利への意欲が強いし、チームのために良い結果を残したいという思いも同じだ」と述べた。

何らかの取り決めが文書化されたのかとの質問には「されていない。次のレースまでの時間が限られていたからだ。２日で物事を変えることはできない。今後どうすればより良くできるか、いずれ話し合うことになるだろう」と語った。

一方、イタリアＧＰをクラッシュによりリタイアしたルクレールは記者団に対し、レース後に映像を確認した結果、自身の動きが行き過ぎだったと認め、「ルイスにもそう伝えた。今回の件が私たちの良好な関係に悪影響を及ぼすことは決してなかったし、今後も影響することはない」と語った。

items.title: Philippine rescuers resume search for survivors of Palawan ferry fire
items.author: Karen Lema
items.creator: Karen Lema
items.summary: Philippine rescuers on Friday resumed the search for survivors of a ferry fire that killed at least five people off the western province of Palawan, with more than 80 people still missing.
items.body:
Philippine rescuers on Friday resumed the search for survivors of a ferry fire that killed at least five people off the western province of Palawan, with more than 80 people still missing.
Rescue operations were complicated by thick smoke still emanating from the burned vessel, preventing responders from boarding the ferry, Cayabyab, spokesperson for the Philippine Coast Guard, said.
Cayabyab said the number of missing was revised to 84 from 86 after authorities verified that two people originally listed on the manifest had not been on board. The number of people rescued stood at 43.
Richard Marceliano, one of the survivors, told GMA News that he saw a small amount of smoke that quickly turned into a raging fire and spread through the ferry within seconds. He said he and other passengers spent nearly two hours floating in the sea before they were rescued.
The Coast Guard has deployed five vessels and divers to the area, while army rescue boats, fishermen and private resort owners continued to assist in the search that began Wednesday night. Cayabyab said a larger Coast Guard vessel would also be deployed.
It remained unclear what triggered the blaze. A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), citing survivor accounts, said two successive explosions were heard from within the ship, which triggered the fire.
According to the vessel's manifest, the ferry was carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members on a voyage from Baseco in Manila to Coron, a popular tourist destination in Palawan known for its diving sites and island-hopping attractions.
The ferry was also carrying five motorcycles, an electric vehicle, a forklift, a pickup truck and mostly cargo goods, according to the Coast Guard.

items.title: Russian air strikes injure two, cause fire in 9-storey apartment building in Kyiv, officials say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian air strikes injured two and caused a fire in a nine-storey apartment building in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv on Friday morning, the city authorities said on Telegram, after they asked people to seek shelter amid a drone alert.
items.body:
Russian air strikes injured two and caused a fire in a nine-storey apartment building in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv on Friday morning, the city authorities said on Telegram, after they asked people to seek shelter amid a drone alert.
Separately, Ukrainian drones damaged civilian infrastructure in the Russian city of Saratov on the Volga River, regional governor Roman Busargin said on Telegram, adding that there were no casualties.
The Saratov region, a frequent target of Ukrainian air strikes, including [USN:P8N441021 TEXT:"an attack"] earlier this week, is home to a large oil refinery run by state oil company Rosneft (ROSN.MM) , as well as a number of other industrial and military facilities.
Reuters could not immediately verify the reports. Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.

items.title: 米半導体アルテラ、年内ＩＰＯ準備　20億ドル超調達も＝関係筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Milana Vinn　Echo Wang

[ニューヨーク １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Milana Vinn　Echo Wang

[ニューヨーク １０日 ロイター] - 関係者によると、米投資ファンドのシルバーレイクと米半導体大手インテルが支援する米半導体メーカーのアルテラは、早ければ年内の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を目指して準備を進めている。調達額は２０億ドル以上となる可能性があり、半導体業界ではここ数年で最大規模のＩＰＯとなる見込みだ。

シルバーレイクは、アルテラのＩＰＯの引受先として、バークレイズ、シティ、ＪＰモルガン、モルガン・スタンレーを選定した。

カリフォルニア州サンノゼに本社を置くアルテラは、今後数週間以内にＩＰＯの非公開申請を行う準備を進めているが、ＩＰＯの時期や規模を含む計画は依然として変更される可能性があるという。

アルテラ、バークレイズ、ＪＰモルガン、モルガン・スタンレー、シルバーレイクはコメントを控えた。シティとインテルはコメント要請に直ちには回答しなかった。

今回のＩＰＯは、２３年に約５０億ドルを調達して上場した英半導体設計大手アーム・ホールディングス以来、半導体業界で最大規模のＩＰＯの一つとなる見込みだ。

アルテラは、通信機器から軍事用途まで、様々な目的に使用できるプログラマブルチップを製造している。同社の製品は、データセンター、通信ネットワーク、産業用機器、航空宇宙・防衛システム、および人工知能（ＡＩ）アプリケーションなどで利用されている。

同社は１５年にインテルに約１６７億ドルで買収されたが、インテルがシルバーレイクに５１％の株式を４４億６０００万ドルで売却することに合意し、企業価値が８７億５０００万ドルと評価されたことを受け、昨年９月に完全な独立企業となった。インテルは４９％の株式を保有し続けている。

アルテラのラギーブ・フセイン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は以前から、株式公開を目指す意向を示していた。

２０２２年２月撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Florence Lo/Illustration）

Milana Vinn　Echo Wang

[ニューヨーク １０日 ロイター] - 関係者によると、米投資ファンドのシルバーレイクと米半導体大手インテルが支援する米半導体メーカーのアルテラは、早ければ年内の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を目指して準備を進めている。調達額は２０億ドル以上となる可能性があり、半導体業界ではここ数年で最大規模のＩＰＯとなる見込みだ。

シルバーレイクは、アルテラのＩＰＯの引受先として、バークレイズ、シティ、ＪＰモルガン、モルガン・スタンレーを選定した。

カリフォルニア州サンノゼに本社を置くアルテラは、今後数週間以内にＩＰＯの非公開申請を行う準備を進めているが、ＩＰＯの時期や規模を含む計画は依然として変更される可能性があるという。

アルテラ、バークレイズ、ＪＰモルガン、モルガン・スタンレー、シルバーレイクはコメントを控えた。シティとインテルはコメント要請に直ちには回答しなかった。

今回のＩＰＯは、２３年に約５０億ドルを調達して上場した英半導体設計大手アーム・ホールディングス以来、半導体業界で最大規模のＩＰＯの一つとなる見込みだ。

アルテラは、通信機器から軍事用途まで、様々な目的に使用できるプログラマブルチップを製造している。同社の製品は、データセンター、通信ネットワーク、産業用機器、航空宇宙・防衛システム、および人工知能（ＡＩ）アプリケーションなどで利用されている。

同社は１５年にインテルに約１６７億ドルで買収されたが、インテルがシルバーレイクに５１％の株式を４４億６０００万ドルで売却することに合意し、企業価値が８７億５０００万ドルと評価されたことを受け、昨年９月に完全な独立企業となった。インテルは４９％の株式を保有し続けている。

アルテラのラギーブ・フセイン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は以前から、株式公開を目指す意向を示していた。

items.title: Tencent-backed Enflame triples in Shanghai debut as China AI chip bets surge
items.author: Yantoultra Ngui, Samuel Shen
items.creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Samuel Shen
items.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence chipmaker Shanghai Enflame Technology surged about 200% in its Shanghai debut on Friday, after the Tencent-backed company raised 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million) in its initial public offering.
items.body:
Chinese artificial intelligence chipmaker Shanghai Enflame Technology (688801.SS) surged about 200% in its Shanghai debut on Friday, after the [USN:L1N44U0IH TEXT:"Tencent-backed"] company raised 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million) in its initial public offering.
The stock opened at 410 yuan versus its offer price of 142.18 yuan, and rose to as high as 475 yuan before slipping back to around 430 yuan. China's STAR Market dropped more than 2%, while the CSI 300 Index (.CSI300) was down 1.43%.
Enflame's debut adds to a rush of [USN:L4N42H0N2 TEXT:"listings"] by Chinese companies seeking to supply computing chips for artificial intelligence, as Beijing pushes for home-grown alternatives to U.S. suppliers such as Nvidia (NVDA.O) .
"Currently, subscription for new shares in the A-share market is one of the few investment approaches that can bring definite returns to investors," said Shen Meng, director at Beijing-based boutique investment bank Chanson & Co.
He said GPU-related businesses offered investors clearer growth prospects than some concept stocks with weaker fundamentals, while U.S. restrictions on Chinese access to advanced chips have increased interest in domestic alternatives.
Enflame is one of a group of Chinese AI chip startups sometimes called the "four little GPU dragons", alongside Moore Threads (688795.SS) , MetaX (688802.SS) and Biren Technology (6082.HK) .
Enflame sold 43.04 million new shares, equal to 10% of its enlarged share capital, on Shanghai's tech-focused STAR Market.
Its offer price gave it a market value of about 61.2 billion yuan, according to its [USN:L1N4510EJ TEXT:"filing"] on Wednesday.
At around 430 yuan on Friday, Enflame's market value had jumped to roughly 185 billion yuan, more than triple the valuation at the IPO price.
Tencent (0700.HK) is Enflame's largest shareholder, with a 17.95% stake after the offering, and was also the company's largest customer before the listing.
Sales linked to Tencent accounted for 83.79% of Enflame's 2025 revenue, its prospectus showed.
Enflame has yet to turn a profit. Its net loss narrowed to 1.16 billion yuan in 2025 from 1.51 billion yuan a year earlier, while revenue rose 37% to 990.2 million yuan, the prospectus showed.
The company forecast revenue of 2.3 billion yuan to 3 billion yuan for the first nine months of 2026, alongside a net loss of 700 million yuan to 860 million yuan.
It expects to break even or become profitable in 2026 or 2027, depending on revenue growth and margins, the filing [USN:L1N4510EJ TEXT:"showed"].
The company plans to use most of the proceeds to develop its fifth- and sixth-generation AI chips, related software and large scale computing systems, according to its prospectus.
($1 = 6.7061 Chinese yuan)

items.title: 日銀の今月利上げを全員が予想、次は来年1月が約6割で最多ーサーベイ
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 日本銀行による利上げペースが加速するとの見方が市場で広がる中、すべての日銀ウオッチャーが今月の金融政策決定会合で政策金利を引き上げ、約6割が来年1月に追加利上げを行うとみている。

ブルームバーグがエコノミスト52人を対象に4－10日に行った調査によると、17、18日の次回会合で政策金利を1.0%程度から1.25%程度に引き上げると全員が予想した。その次の利上げは58%が来年1月を、35%が今年12月を見込んでいる。10月会合でも連続で利上げするとの見方はなかった。

ニッセイ基礎研究所の上野剛志主席エコノミストは、9月会合での利上げを「ほぼ既定路線」とみる。先行きの利上げペースや景気を刺激も抑制もしない中立金利までの距離感をポイントに挙げ、「これらに関して植田和男総裁がどのように発言するかが注目だ」という。

複数の関係者によると、日銀は今月会合で政策金利を0.25ポイント引き上げ、1.25%とする公算だ。中東情勢やAI関連需要、これまでの円安進行などで物価の上振れリスクが引き続き意識される中、先行きの利上げペースも柔軟に対応する。

今後の利上げペースに関する問いでは、四半期に1回程度との回答が46%で最多となり、次いで4ー5カ月に1回程度が36%となった。7月会合前に実施した前回調査では、半年に1回程度との見方が82%を占めており、急速に短縮が進んだ。

背景には、植田総裁が7月会合後の会見で利上げペース加速の可能性に言及したことがあるが、いわゆる「外圧」を挙げる声も少なくない。7月会合の直後に日米の通貨当局が協調して円買いの為替市場介入に踏み切って以降、ベッセント米財務長官による日銀の利上げに期待感を示す発言が続いているためだ。

シティグループ証券の中村颯介エコノミストは、協調介入を経て日米当局の円安けん制は新たな局面に入ったとし、来年末までに日銀は2%まで利上げするとみている。米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB)が利上げサイクルに入る場合は、日銀の政策金利の最高到達点（ターミナルレート）も「2%を超える可能性が高まる」という。

items.title: Taiwan's vice president on rare Europe visit for Italy democracy forum
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Taiwan Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim is making a rare visit to Europe, attending a forum on democracy in Italy along with Taipei's foreign minister, the presidential office said on Friday.
items.body:
Taiwan Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim is making a rare visit to Europe, attending a forum on democracy in Italy along with Taipei's foreign minister, the presidential office said on Friday.
While Taiwan's foreign ministers on occasion visit Europe and other parts of the world that have no formal ties to the Chinese-claimed island, it is rare for an official as senior as the vice president to do so, given the risk of a backlash from Beijing against the host nation.
China says Taiwan is one of its provinces, a view the democratically-governed island strongly rejects.
Hsiao has been invited to attend the Ventotene Conference for Freedom and Democracy, and is travelling with Taiwan Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung, the presidential office said in a brief statement.
Other details will be provided once she returns to Taiwan, it added.
Neither China nor Italy's foreign ministries immediately responded to requests for comment.
The Ventotene conference takes place from Thursday until Saturday this week.
Early on Friday Asia time, Pina Picierno, Vice-President of the European Parliament, announced on her Facebook page that Hsiao was attending the conference, saying her presence had been kept secret until her arrival to protect her participation. ﻿
Italy, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic ties to Chinese-claimed Taiwan.
Last November, Hsiao spoke at the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China's annual summit, held in the European Parliament in [USN:L4N3WK05T TEXT:"Brussels"].
Taiwan has sought closer ties with Europe, especially since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. Europe has its own disputes with China, over both trade imbalances and also its criticism of what it sees as Chinese support for Russia.
Hsiao, a fluent English speaker, has previously been sanctioned by China for being an "independence diehard".
Taiwan's government says only the island's people can decide their future.

items.title: UEFA urges US court to deny FIFA subsidiaries' bid to join Infantino discovery fight
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: UEFA urged a U.S. court on Thursday to reject an attempt by FIFA's American subsidiaries to intervene in its bid to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his abandoned World Cup commercial-rights plan.
items.body:
UEFA urged a U.S. court on Thursday to reject an attempt by FIFA's American subsidiaries to intervene in its bid to obtain evidence for a potential Swiss criminal case against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his abandoned World Cup commercial-rights plan.
In a filing in Manhattan federal court, European soccer's governing body said FIFA (Americas) Inc and FWC2026 US Inc were improperly trying to act as stand-ins for FIFA and Infantino, neither of whom has sought to join the case.
UEFA said its request under a U.S. discovery law seeks documents and testimony from Thrive Capital Management and its founder Joshua Kushner, who it says may hold information about the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise transaction.
The plan, which Infantino withdrew on August 1 after a backlash from soccer bodies and other critics, envisaged selling a permanent stake in commercial and operational rights connected to the World Cup and other FIFA events to private investors.
UEFA CONSIDERING CRIMINAL COMPLAINT AGAINST INFANTINO UEFA has said it is considering filing a criminal complaint in Switzerland alleging criminal mismanagement by Infantino and potentially other FIFA officials. Infantino and FIFA have not been charged with wrongdoing.
FIFA accused UEFA last week of running a "[USN:L6N44V17M TEXT:"smear campaign"]" and characterized the discovery applications as a fishing expedition intended to damage FIFA and its leadership.
FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Infantino has denied doing anything wrong.
In Thursday's response, UEFA said the subsidiaries had no direct legal interest in the New York proceeding because they were not targets of the contemplated Swiss case and were not recipients of the proposed subpoenas.
It said the confidentiality concerns cited by the U.S. subsidiaries belonged, if to anyone, to their Swiss parent, FIFA. UEFA also argued that Thrive and Kushner already have lawyers who can challenge any subpoenas after they are served.
Thrive did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Thrive founder Kushner is the brother of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of U.S. President Donald Trump.
UEFA said granting the subsidiaries a role before the court rules would depart from the usual process for requests under Section 1782, which are commonly granted initially without opposition and then tested through motions to quash.
The European body argued that the subsidiaries' intervention would create unnecessary delay by adding another round of merits briefing before UEFA could seek the records.
The court has not yet ruled on either UEFA's discovery application or the intervention motion.

items.title: Cowboys signing TE Brevyn Spann-Ford to 3-year extension
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Dallas Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford has agreed to a three-year contract extension for $18 million with $12.075 million guaranteed, NFL Network reported on Thursday.
items.body:
Dallas Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford has agreed to a three-year contract extension for $18 million with $12.075 million guaranteed, NFL Network reported on Thursday.
The Cowboys did not disclose financial terms in announcing the extension for Spann-Ford, who could have been a restricted free agent after the 2026 season and now will be under contract through 2029. He was due to count $1,090,847 against the salary cap this season, according to Spotrac.
Spann-Ford, 26, went undrafted out of the University of Minnesota in 2024. The Cowboys use him as primarily a blocking tight end and special teams player.
He played in 17 games last season with five starts and caught nine of 13 targets for 90 yards and one touchdown. He played on 300 offensive snaps (25%) and 243 special teams snaps (50%) last season.
Spann-Ford appeared in all 34 games for Dallas the past two seasons and totaled 18 receptions on 27 targets for 178 yards, one touchdown and 10 first downs.
He is teamed with two-time Pro Bowl selection Jake Ferguson, who is more of a receiving tight end.
--Field Level Media

items.title: サッカー＝モロッコ、30年Ｗ杯決勝開催を発表　ＦＩＦＡは明言せず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１０日　ロイター］ - モロッコ・サッカー連盟のフージ・レクジャ会長は１０日、２０３０年ワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）の決勝戦が同国で開催されると述べた。スペイン通信社ＥＦＥが報じた。

ＥＦＥによれば、レクジャ会長は政党イベントで、「（カサブランカ近郊の）ベンスリマンが２０３０年Ｗ杯決勝の開催地となる名誉を担うことになる」と語った。

国際サッカー連盟（ＦＩＦＡ）は決勝の開催地を正式発表しておらず、スペインとモロッコが開催権を巡って激しい争いを展開中。ＦＩＦＡの広報担当者は「決定はしかるべき時期にＦＩＦＡによって下される」と述べた。

ベンスリマンはカサブランカから６０キロ離れた都市で、Ｗ杯に向けて建設中の「ハッサン２世スタジアム」の建設地でもある。同スタジアムは収容人数１１万５０００人を予定しており、完成すれば世界最大のサッカー専用スタジアムとなる。

３０年Ｗ杯はモロッコ、ポルトガル、スペインの３カ国が大部分を主催するが、開幕戦を含む最初の３試合はアルゼンチン、パラグアイ、ウルグアイで開催。史上初めて３大陸の６カ国で開催される異例の大会となる。

items.title: 円高恐れる世界の投資家、キャリー取引解消で半導体株安の延長戦警戒
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 世界の株式投資家も、為替市場で円高が加速するリスクを警戒し始めている。これまでの円安を需給面で支えたキャリートレードの巻き戻しが活発化すると資産横断的な投資マネーの逆流が起き、今年前半の相場を盛り上げたAI・半導体関連株の調整が長引く恐れがあるからだ。

日本の超低金利、円安が長らく定着していた中で世界の投資家は調達コストの低い円を借り入れ、高いリターンが見込める米国や新興国の資産を買うキャリートレードを積極的に行ってきた。しかし、ひとたび円高に振れると借入金の返済コストが上がるため、これまでの持ち高を解消せざるを得なくなる。

7月末に日米政府が協調して円買い介入を行っても押し上げ効果は一時的で、再び160円台の円安方向に戻していた円相場が一変したのは先週だ。ベッセント米財務長官が円安を止めるために日本政府や日本銀行が行動することを求める発言を繰り返し、日銀の9月利上げ観測や年金積立金管理運用独立行政法人（GPIF）による資産配分見直しへの期待を強める要因になった。

円は8日に対ドルで一時152円89銭と2月以来の高値に上昇。わずか4日間で7円超、5%近く円高に振れたため、市場ではキャリートレード解消への懸念が増大。米商品先物取引委員会（CFTC）のデータによると、9月1日時点の投資筋の円売り越しポジションは11万枚超と1週間前から3割以上増えていた。

KBC証券のグローバル株式部門責任者、アンドレア・ガベローネ氏は円の「投機的ポジションは依然高水準であり、世界の株式市場に警告を発するサインとして円はわれわれが注視する唯一の指標だ」と話す。

為替トレーダーらは円高の勢いが今後も続くとの見方を強めており、ヘッジファンドは円相場が年末までに対ドルで150円を割り込むと予想し、期間が長めの一部のオプション取引では140円までの円高・ドル安の進展を想定する。

円の一段高でキャリートレードの解消が加速すれば、損益を確定させたい投資家は最も流動性があり、収益性の高い保有株を売却しなければならず、これは今年前半のパフォーマンスが良かったテクノロジー株の下落圧力になる。1－6月の世界の主要株価指数の上昇率上位は、AI・半導体株の影響力が大きい韓国総合株価指数（KOSPI）が上昇率2倍でトップ、日経平均株価も39%上げた。

items.title: フィンランド、グーグルとＡＩインフラ契約で電力逼迫の恐れ＝野党
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Essi Lehto

[ヘルシンキ １０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Essi Lehto

[ヘルシンキ １０日 ロイター] - フィンランドの野党は１０日、電力不足やエネルギー価格の高騰というリスクを防ぐため、データセンターに対する全国的な許可制度を導入すべきだと訴えた。米アルファベット傘下のグーグルが前日、同国への大規模な新規投資を発表したことを受けたもの。

北欧地域は、涼しい気候、豊富な低炭素電力、そして信頼性の高い送電網のおかげで、長年にわたりデータセンターの集積地となってきたが、人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業は現在、消費者や政治家からの厳しい目にさらされている。

グーグルは９日、今後２年間でフィンランドのＡＩインフラに少なくとも１３０億ユーロ（１５１億ドル）を投じると発表した。これは同社にとって欧州最大の投資であり、原子力発電の供給契約も含まれている。

野党第２党の中央党のカイッコネン党首はロイターに対し、フィンランドではデータセンターの立地は歓迎されているものの、同国はそれらを稼働させるのに十分な電力と送電容量を確保しなければならないと語った。

その上で「新たなデータセンター投資のための全国的な許可制度が必要になるだろう。現時点で全体像を本当に把握している者は誰もいない」と述べた。

４月に予定されている総選挙を控え、世論調査で首位を走る社会民主党は、データセンターへの投資を歓迎する一方で、電力需要への影響については依然として懸念を抱いていると表明した。

グーグルの契約には、フィンランドのロビーサ原子力発電所の発電量の最大５０％を２２年間にわたり購入する契約が含まれており、これにより同発電所の稼働予定期間が、当初の２０３０年の閉鎖予定から５０年まで延長されることになった。

フィンランドで原発を運営するフォータムとグーグルは、同国における新たな原子力・再生可能エネルギー開発についても検討していくと発表した。

フィンランド政府はコメント要請に直ちには回答しなかった。

items.title: 世界的な債券売り、米10年債利回り5%目前－CPIに市場は注目
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 債券の弱気派は、来週の米利上げ観測を左右する米インフレ指標の発表を前に、指標となる米10年国債利回りを注目の5%に向けて押し上げている。

米10年債利回りは今週18ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp=0.01%）上昇し、心理的節目の5%に迫る水準に達している。この水準は押し目買いを呼び込む可能性がある一方、一段の売りを誘発し、世界の市場に波及するリスクもある。11日は4.96%と2023年以来の高水準に達し、07年以来の最高水準に近づいている。

利回り急上昇の背景には、原油高に加え、インフレ率が米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の目標を5年にわたり上回る中、市場参加者が対応を迫られていることがある。11日発表の米消費者物価指数（CPI）はここ数年で最も重要な指標の1つとなる見通し。市場では16日の連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）会合で利上げが決まる確率を約70%織り込んでいる。

INGグループの米州調査責任者パドレイク・ガービー氏は「米10年債利回りが5%に達するのは、ここまで来ると予想というより不可避のように見える」と述べ、「債券市場にとって懸念すべき時期だ」と語った。

FRBの金利政策の影響をより受けやすい米2年債利回りは今週、一時4.59%まで上昇した。30年債利回りは07年以来の高水準となり、同債の入札では際立って強い需要を呼び込んだ。

こうした動きは世界の債券市場にも波及している。オーストラリアの指標国債利回りは11日、11年以来の高水準を付け、日本の同等年限の国債利回りは心理的節目となる3%近辺で取引されている。世界の債券利回りを示す指標は07年以来の高水準にある。

オーストラリア・コモンウェルス銀行の金利ストラテジスト、マイケル・タン氏は「現時点で流れを止められるのは、低めの米CPIとFRBの利上げくらいしか思い浮かばない。それがなければ、金利のロングポジションを安心して持てる人はいないと思う」と指摘。「極めて強いタカ派心理が市場を支配している」と述べた。

items.title: Oil prices set to end week over $100 for first time in nearly 4 months
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Oil prices rose on Friday and both major benchmarks are on track to end the week at over $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuel fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies.
items.body:
Oil prices rose on Friday and both major benchmarks are on track to end the week at over $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuel fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies.
Brent crude futures rose $1.05, or 1%, to $108.68 a barrel by 0045 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 95 cents, also 1%, to $103.45 a barrel. Both benchmarks rose over 6% on Thursday.
On a weekly basis, the benchmarks were trading nearly 13% higher - the steepest gain since the week ended July 17.
Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port of [USN:L6N45203X TEXT:"Mocha"] on Thursday, posing a further threat to Red Sea traffic, while Gulf traffic remains restricted through the [USN:L1N452038 TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] as tanker attacks in the region [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"have intensified"] in recent days.
Attacks from Yemen on Saudi energy facilities marked an escalation beyond Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, and raised fears of prolonged disruptions in the broader region, analysts say.
U.S. President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45202Q TEXT:"warned"] the U.S. may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, located near its heavily damaged Natanz uranium enrichment facility, and said the war would end after the November midterm elections.
"With events spiralling and Iran showing it is willing to stretch this conflict as wide and as long as it can, it is becoming increasingly likely that WTI crude will retest the $119.48 high from early March," IG analyst Tony Sycamore said.
Iran said it had [USN:L6N451042 TEXT:"attacked"] 10 ships near the strait on Wednesday, after the U.S. hit five Iranian oil tankers. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it would escalate its response to any further attacks.
The U.S. national average price of diesel surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever on Thursday, according to price tracker GasBuddy, as the U.S.-Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russia's refineries have squeezed supply.
Analysts said the rally's durability will hinge on China, the world's largest crude importer. If China continues to buy, it could amplify the impact of supply disruptions and drive prices higher.
OPEC lowered its forecast for [USN:L6N4520RP TEXT:"world oil demand growth"] in 2026 to 380,000 barrels per day, a copy of its monthly report showed, marking the fifth straight downward revision. [USN:L6N4520MS TEXT:"OPEC oil output"] fell by 640,000 bpd in August, a Reuters survey found.

items.title: Dollar holds gains, yen slips as Mideast energy shock deepens
items.author: Gregor Hunter
items.creator: Gregor Hunter
items.summary: The dollar held near its highest levels of the past week and the yen slipped for a second day at the start of Asian trading on Friday as renewed fears of energy supply disruptions in the Middle East pushed up bond yields and oil prices.
items.body:
The dollar held near its highest levels of the past week and the yen slipped for a second day at the start of Asian trading on Friday as renewed fears of energy supply disruptions in the Middle East pushed up bond yields and oil prices.
The U.S. dollar index , which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 99.081, holding steady after gaining 0.3% on Thursday to reach its highest level since September 7. The rise followed the release of data showing [USN:L1N4520JQ TEXT:"U.S. producer prices"] increased 0.4% in August, meeting market expectations as energy prices rebounded during the month.
"The safe-haven U.S. dollar gained on risk-aversion flows, helped by higher energy prices that have lifted the chance of a Fed hike next week to 70%," said Tony Sycamore, market analyst at IG in Sydney.
Energy prices extended gains into a sixth day, with Brent crude futures rising 1.2% to $108.96 a barrel as trading resumed in Asia.
Both major benchmarks breached the $100 mark earlier this week, with WTI futures [USN:L1N45201P TEXT:"surging"] across the threshold on Thursday for the first time since May 21 after [USN:L6N45203X TEXT:"Iran-aligned Houthis"] seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands.
Against the yen , the U.S. dollar was as much as 0.1% firmer at 154.615 yen, while the euro strengthened by a similar magnitude to as much as 179.49 yen after the European Central Bank [USN:L1N452054 TEXT:"hiked interest rates"] on Thursday for the second time this year.
But the Japanese currency regained some strength after data released on Friday showed [USN:L4N4521UO TEXT:"wholesale inflation"] rose 7.6% in August from a year earlier, bolstering the case for a rate hike this month.
The Australian dollar was flat at $0.7160, while its kiwi counterpart was up 0.1% at $0.5805.
Both the euro and the British pound were level against the dollar at $1.1613 and $1.3510, respectively.
PRESSURE BUILDS ON FEDERAL RESERVE Markets are awaiting the release of U.S. CPI data later on Friday, one of the last [USN:L1N4520IJ TEXT:"major economic data points"] released before the Federal Reserve meets next week.
Fed funds futures are pricing an implied 71.3% probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the U.S. central bank's next two-day meeting ending on September 16, compared to a 61.2% chance in the previous trading session, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Fixed-income markets remained uneasy after the U.S. Treasury Department tripled the size of its [USN:L1N4520U7 TEXT:"long-dated bond repurchase"], with a gauge of bond volatility (.MOVE) rising to its highest level in a month. The yield on U.S. 10-year government bonds was up 2.3 basis points at 4.965%.
"10-year U.S. Treasury yields are within striking distance of 5%, as the markets have reassessed the Fed's path higher while term premium is appropriately hovering near pre-GFC levels," Barclays analysts wrote. "We remain of the view that bonds are not cheap yet and catalysts for a rally do not appear imminent."
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was down 0.8% at $76,624.32, while ether declined by a similar magnitude to $2,443.18.

items.title: 米最高裁、ミズーリ州の共和党作成新選挙区割りの使用を阻止
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrew Chung

[１０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Andrew Chung

[１０日 ロイター] - 米連邦最高裁判所は１０日、１１月の中間選挙で共和党に有利となるよう作成されたミズーリ州の連邦下院選挙区の新たな区割りについて、使用を差し止める判断を示した。トランプ大統領および共和党にとって打撃となり、同党が連邦下院でかろうじて確保している過半数を維持できるかどうかにも影響を与えそうだ。

最高裁判事らは、この選挙区割りに異議を唱える緊急申し立てを認め、１１月３日の中間選挙で再編後の選挙区のみを使用することを認めた連邦地裁判事の決定を差し止めた。

これは、ミズーリ州の連邦下院選挙区を巡り州裁判所と連邦裁判所の双方で繰り広げられた全面的な法廷闘争の中で、共和党が作成した区割りの維持を求める申し立てを連邦最高裁が退けたものであり、３日間で２度目の判断となった。

ミズーリ州の共和党は２０２５年、民主党の連邦下院議員を長年務めてきたエマニュエル・クリーバー氏の地盤であるカンザスシティーを中心とした選挙区を解体する新たな区割りを採択した。これは、共和党候補に有利となるよう選挙区を再編するという、トランプ氏が支援するより広範な取り組みの一環だった。

１０日の最高裁の判断を受け共和党当局者らは、中間選挙は２０２２年に制定された従来の選挙区割りに基づいて実施されると述べた。彼らは以前、この結果になれば１１月の選挙を適法かつ適時に実施する能力が損なわれると警告していた。

異議申立人には、共和党作成の選挙区割りに反対する団体も含まれており、ミズーリ州セントルイスを拠点とする連邦地裁首席判事スティーブン・クラーク氏が８日に判断を下した直後、最高裁による介入を求めていた。

クラーク判事の判断は、ミズーリ州当局が再編区割りの復活を求めた別の申し立てについて、保守派のブレット・カバノー連邦最高裁判事が単独で介入を拒否した直後に出された。この再編区割りは、住民投票により承認されるまで発効しないと州最高裁が判断していた。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝大谷がＩＬ入りへ、最短復帰はポストシーズン開始6日前
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１０日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ドジャースのデーブ・ロバーツ監督は９日の試合後、左膝と右上腕二頭筋に問題を抱える大谷翔平選手を負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）に入れると発表した。

大谷はここ７試合のうち６試合でスタメン落ち。出場した直近７試合では２６打数２安打、長打なし、打点なしという成績にとどまっていた。投手としては７月３日を最後に登板していない。

ロバーツ監督は「もし明日がポストシーズンの試合なら、大谷はラインナップに入っていただろう」とコメント。今回のＩＬ入りはポストシーズンを見据えてのものと位置付け、「そのころにはきょうよりもずっと良い状態になっているはずだ。万全の状態になるかと言えば、おそらくそうではないだろう。しかし、今は休養期間を取ることでシーズンを最後まで戦い抜き、その先へ進むための状態には十分になれると考えている」と語った。

大谷の戦列復帰は最短で９月２３日。ポストシーズンは、ドジャースがワイルドカードシリーズに回ることになれば同２９日から開始となる。

またロバーツ監督によると、ドジャースは大谷のＩＬ入りに伴って若手有望株のホスエ・デパウラ外野手（２１）を昇格させる予定。デパウラは今季、２Ａで１２４試合に出場して打率３割３厘、２７本塁打、１０４打点、１０６得点、３１盗塁、ＯＰＳ（出塁率＋長打率）０．９４８をマークしている。
